Design: Quill invoice agent for Ledgerly Cloud tenants. Version for review.
Step read_invoice: the model reads input and proposes; it causes no effect itself.
Step pay (payment): decided by deterministic code. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Destination comes from the payee and contact registry.
Step bank_change (bank change): decided by rules with a named owner. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Destination comes from the payee and contact registry.
Step email (send email): decided by deterministic code. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Destination comes from the payee and contact registry.
Step run_report_code (execute code): decided by deterministic code. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Code runs on the narrowed sandbox rung with no network.
Credentials: no credential is placed in the model's context; each task gets its own short-lived token.
Tools: the loadout is computed per task, and it narrows when an untrusted document enters context. Third-party MCP tool descriptions and schemas are pinned.
Model files: formats that can run code on load are refused; files are checked against a model bill signed by a named person.
Egress: outbound mail goes only to an allow-list of domains and recipients.
Approvals: each approval is bound to the digest of the exact effect; the reviewer sees the full rendered facts.
Agents: 3 agents; they hand off typed messages whose grant can only shrink.
Memory: writes carry trust labels.
Evidence: chained, anchored to an outside service, with the examiner's fields.
Budgets per task: 12 model calls, 3 sends, 3 identical repeats.
Degradation: model provider missing -> hold; bank feed missing -> queue; registry missing -> deny; anchor service missing -> queue; detector missing -> fallback_owned.
Release gate: strict per-step comparison against baseline runs, with an anchor to the first release, new-hit rule on.
Monitor amount detector: raises alerts for a person; owner Ian; about 1.5 alerts a week; the owner can read about 10.
Monitor extractor confidence: raises alerts for a person; owner security; about 4 alerts a week; the owner can read about 10.
Baseline amount detector: acknowledged within 7 days, retuned every 91 days.
Waivers: W03 detector shed cap owned by Ian, review on day 300.
Recurring jobs: 30 in the register; each has an owner and a different backup; each leaves a dated artefact.
Control listed in the security summary: money path M1-M8.
Incident cases: cannot close with a blank owner or deadline; notices are recorded in the sealed chain.
External claims: claims are stated with their evidence level.
Marker scan: a signal for review, not a control.

Step pay (payment): decided by deterministic code. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Destination comes from the payee and contact registry.
Step bank_change (bank change): decided by rules with a named owner. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Destination comes from the payee and contact registry.
Step email (send email): decided by deterministic code. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Destination comes from the payee and contact registry.
Step run_report_code (execute code): decided by deterministic code. It passes the gate before execution. If the gate errors, the step is held. Code runs on the narrowed sandbox rung with no network.
Credentials: no credential is placed in the model's context; one standing token is reused across tasks.
Tools: the loadout is computed per task, and it narrows when an untrusted document enters context. Third-party MCP tool descriptions and schemas are pinned.
Model files: formats that can run code on load are refused; files are checked against a model bill signed by a named person.
Egress: outbound mail goes only to an allow-list of domains and recipients.
Approvals: each approval is bound to the digest of the exact effect; the reviewer sees the full rendered facts.
Agents: 3 agents; they hand off typed messages whose grant can only shrink.
Memory: writes carry trust labels.
Evidence: chained, anchored to an outside service, with the examiner's fields.
Budgets per task: 12 model calls, 3 sends, 3 identical repeats.
Degradation: model provider missing -> hold; bank feed missing -> queue; registry missing -> deny; anchor service missing -> queue; detector missing -> fallback_owned.
Release gate: per-step comparison with margins (total 40, axis 20), no anchor to the first release, new-hit rule on.
Monitor amount detector: raises alerts for a person; owner Ian; about 1.5 alerts a week; the owner can read about 10.
Monitor extractor confidence: raises alerts for a person; owner security; about 4 alerts a week; the owner can read about 10.
Baseline amount detector: acknowledged within 7 days, retuned every 91 days.
Waivers: W03 detector shed cap owned by Ian, review on day 300.
Recurring jobs: 30 in the register; each has an owner and a different backup; each leaves a dated artefact.
Control listed in the security summary: money path M1-M8.
Incident cases: cannot close with a blank owner or deadline; notices are recorded in the sealed chain.
External claims: claims are stated with their evidence level.
Marker scan: a signal for review, not a control.
